items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Right, trombone player named Snub Mosely and Chester Clark, trumpet player, alto player named Lee Hilliard and James Jeter, and Hayes Pillars and Charles Pillars.

ctx.x: So, for the record, we’ll state that contrary to what’s been written you never played with Alphonso Trent’s band but there were some members left from that band that you played with.
Right, trombone player named Snub Mosely and Chester Clark, trumpet player, alto player named Lee Hilliard and James Jeter, and Hayes Pillars and Charles Pillars.
Was Snub Mosely playing his slide saxophone even then?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: And they had a fellow named Charles Pillars. Both of them played in the band.

ctx.x: Where did they get those names from? Were they Mexicans or something?

No, Pillar -- they were black. Jeeter was very light. He was very light. His name was James Jeeter. And the tenor play was named Hays Pillars. And they had a fellow named Charles Pillars. Both of them played in the band. But they stressed -- not like the Benny Moten style, not like Hot Lips was playing or not like McKinney's Cotton Pickers. We had a job in a club so consequently, we had to play a lot of --
